title: perf-regression-triage-guide
content:
Purpose:
This is the working runbook for performance regression tracking and alert triage for the Serving Runtime team. It captures our standard dashboards, initial investigative steps, bisect guidance, and canary vs baseline comparison checklist. Goal: reduce mean time to root cause (MTTR) for perf regressions and make canary decisions consistent and reproducible.

Scope:
- Latency/throughput regressions for hosted + dedicated runtime (text generation & chat endpoints)
- Regressions caused by code changes, model swaps, infra changes (drivers, CUDA, libs), and config flips (batching, kv cache, quantization)
- Not intended for model quality regressions (see evals team playbook)

On-call responsibilities:
- First responder: oncall-runtime (Slack #eng-runtime-oncall). Acknowledge alerts within 10 minutes.
- Escalation: if triage needs infra or SRE (drivers, node failures) ping #sre and @oncall-sre.
- Communicate: short incident thread in #eng-runtime and add a brief note to the incident doc template (link above).

Key dashboards & panels (start here):
- Grafana: Serving Runtime · Perf Overview (panel: p50/p95/p99 latency by route)
- Grafana: Serving Runtime · Throughput & Tokens/sec (by model & instance type)
- Grafana: Worker · GPU Utilization & Memory (per node)
- Grafana: Batching · Batch size distribution & queue latency
- Grafana: Cache · KV cache hit rate & miss latency
- Datadog traces: endpoint flamegraphs (search by request id)

Primary metrics + alert thresholds (examples):
- p95 latency increase > 30% vs baseline (30m window) -> warn
- p99 latency increase > 40% or absolute > 3s -> page
- Throughput drop > 25% with concurrent request volume constant -> page
- GPU utilization spike > 85% sustained for 5m without throughput increase -> warn/page depending on user impact
- KV cache hit rate drop > 20% -> warn
Note: thresholds are tuned per-customer on dedicated pools. See per-customer dashboard links in customer pages.

Initial triage checklist (first 20 minutes):
1) Confirm alert validity
   - Check Grafana perf-overview, then compare to baseline window (previous 6h and 24h).
   - Look for global vs local scope: single route/model vs all routes.
2) Correlate recent deploys
   - Check deploy history (console rollouts page) and GitHub PRs merged in last 30–60 minutes. Use /deploys?tag=rolling in console.
   - If a canary just rolled, pause/rollback the canary if clear degradation on canary-only routes.
3) Check infra signals
   - Node restarts, driver updates, kernel logs (SRE page). GPU errors: dmesg, nvidia-smi, and node exporter panels.
4) Check batching & queue metrics
   - Sudden change in average batch size or queue latency often explains p95 spikes.
5) KV cache and model variant checks
   - Verify cache hit rate and whether requests are hitting warmed cache. Also confirm model variant/quantization used by the route.
6) Collect sample traces and a few raw request ids for later bisecting.

Bisect guidance (code-level regression suspected):
- Use perf-bisect pipeline (internal) to run A/B builds across a small fleet. High level: bisect-start -> run-requests -> collect-metrics -> bisect-next.
- Requirements: deterministic repro script with replayed prompts, stable dataset (5–10k requests), run at target qps to exercise batching.
- Bisect tip: if noise is high, increase replay volume or reduce parallelism to amplify the regression signal.
- When bisect narrows to a commit, request the author to run a local repro and add a micro-benchmark patch.

Canary vs baseline comparison checklist (when canary reports degradation):
1) Define the comparison window: last 30m of canary vs equal-length baseline before canary start.
2) Metric set for comparison: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, mean batch size, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, error rate (5xx).
3) Statistical test: use bootstrap CI (internal script) to check p95 difference significance; avoid acting on single-minute blips.
4) If canary shows consistent >20–30% increase in p95 and higher p99 tail, fail the canary and rollback.
5) If only p50 changed but p99 stable, consider degraded throughput/batching config changes — continue canary with close monitoring if impact is minor.

Common root causes & quick remediations:
- New kernel/driver/CUDA -> rollback driver or pin nodes; contact SRE for node reimaging
- Batch size policy change -> revert policy or adjust max batch delay
- Model variant or quantization change -> revert to previous variant; run lightweight perf test locally
- KV cache cold start (after scale-up or restart) -> warm cache with synthetic traffic, consider stretch warmup period in autoscaler
- Memory pressure / OOMs -> reduce concurrency, increase instance memory or reduce model shard size

Post-triage steps (follow-up within 48h):
- Open incident ticket with root cause, mitigation, timeline, and learnings (tag: eng-runtime-perf).
- If code change caused regression: include the minimal repro, bisect result, and suggested fix/PR link.
- Update dashboards or alerts if thresholds were too sensitive or blind to root cause.
- Add a unit/perf test to the repo to catch the regression in CI if feasible.

Runbook examples & quick commands:
- Grab traces for request id: curl -sS https://tracing.redwood.local/api/trace?rid=<REQUEST_ID> | jq .
- Compare p95 baseline vs recent (internal script): ./scripts/compare_metrics.py --panel perf-overview --metric p95 --window 30m
- Run perf-bisect (example): ./tools/perf-bisect --commit-range abc123..def456 --replay-corpus tests/replay/corpus-10k.json --qps 50

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- Formalize per-customer alert thresholds in console (owner: Priya).
- Improve automated cache warmup on scale events (owner: Diego).
- Add more tail-latency microbenchmarks to PR CI (owner: Ethan).

Notes & context (informal):
- We often see regressions that only show up at scale due to batching interplay — try to reproduce at target QPS, not locally.
- Prefer conservative canary rules for high-SLA customers; default canaries can be more permissive for early rollout.
- Link to long-running perf experiments and historical baselines: Grafana perf-history dashboard (linked above).

If you have ideas or edits, drop them in this doc or ping me (@aisha) in #eng-runtime.
